_note: Tasks for the Scriptorium. Each is a case where letters are genuinely executable world instructions rather than puzzle tokens — the world state is checked, not a stored answer. `solution` is the sequence the self-test plays through the real UI path, so a task that stops being solvable fails a check rather than a playtest.

tasks.name: The Raising
tasks.brief: Bring the water above the cursor to 7, without touching it.
tasks.teaches: A letter with dots above RAISES what stands over it, and it raises by RUNGS OF THE ABJAD LADDER — 5 to 7 is two rungs, not two units. The number of dots is the number of rungs.

tasks.name: One Body
tasks.brief: Write a word of three letters that holds together as a single body.
tasks.teaches: A written word IS one body here, and the six letters that never join what follows — ا د ذ ر ز و — are where it breaks. That is not doctrine: it is why an Arabic word can look like several pieces on the page. Choose letters that connect.

tasks.name: The Chain of Being
tasks.brief: Three letters must still be standing over the single pier when gravity is turned on. Under the metaphysics you are starting in, this cannot be done.
tasks.teaches: The same three letters are two bodies under one metaphysics and one body under another. Sufi lettrism refuses to SEVER at all — 'the chain of being is not cut' — so a word bonds straight through the break that orthography puts in it. Change the ruleset, not the program.

tasks.name: The Pen
tasks.brief: Something is already standing here. Finish it, then read the world.
tasks.teaches: You have been writing the world all along. It can also be READ — including the parts you did not write. Two letters of a word are standing in front of you; write the third into the gap and the structure resolves into قلم, the Pen. Sūra 68 is named for it, and opens on the letter nūn.
